title: Slab-built cat-shaped planter in air-dry clay
subtitle: A cat-silhouette planter built from slabs with a hollow body for a small pot
excerpt: A cat-shaped planter whose hollow slab body holds a small nursery pot or succulent. The front profile is cut to a seated cat silhouette with pointed ears; the box body behind holds soil or a small plastic pot. No kiln is needed; the finished planter is sealed for indoor use with dry-soil plants only.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Slab-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness, used as the building unit
The drying stage where clay holds its shape but is still damp enough to join pieces
Clay thinned with water, used as adhesive between clay pieces
Fully air-dried and unfired; ready for sealing

content.text: box with a cat-silhouette face panel on the front. A small succulent or cactus sits in a nursery pot dropped into the open top; the cat's open-top head holds the pot in place. Air-dry clay is not waterproof, so the planter suits plants watered with a measured dropper rather than overhead watering. No kiln is needed.

materials.name: Card or paper for cat-silhouette template

content.text: Draw a simple cat silhouette on card: a seated cat with a round head about 8 cm wide, triangular ears 2 cm tall, and a body tapering to a base about 10 cm wide. The total height should be about 14 cm. The interior of the body becomes the planting space; plan for it to be at least 7 cm wide and 7 cm deep at the widest point.
Roll a slab 7 mm thick. Cut the cat-silhouette front panel using the card template and fettling knife. Cut a matching back panel (the same silhouette or a plain rectangle of matching height).
Cut two side walls and a base from the same slab, sized to create an interior depth of 6 to 7 cm between the front and back panels.

Score a simple face on the front panel with the needle tool: two almond-shaped eyes, a small nose, and whisker lines. Do not pierce through. Add ear details by pressing a small curved line inside each ear triangle.
to all joining edges. Assemble side walls to front panel, then back panel, then base. Reinforce inside corners with coils of soft clay.
Leave the top of the body open to accept the plant pot. Smooth all outer joins with a damp rib and sponge.

over three to four days. Apply three coats of PVA inside the planting cavity to add moisture resistance for dry-soil watering. Apply two coats of PVA to all outer surfaces. Paint the front panel face details with acrylic: black, tabby stripe, or tuxedo pattern.

Suitable for succulents and cacti in dry-soil conditions. Do not use overhead watering: drip water directly to the soil with a dropper or syringe. Do not leave standing water in the base. Keep indoors.
Cut a rabbit, fox, or hedgehog silhouette using the same slab-box method.

items.cause: The pointed ear tips dry faster than the body of the front panel
items.fix: Cover the planter loosely with a cloth for the first 24 hours. Repair cracks at leather-hard with fresh slip on both sides of the crack

items.problem: Front panel bows outward during drying
items.cause: The front panel is larger and dries at a different rate from the sides
items.fix: Press the side coil reinforcements larger and deeper at assembly. Support the front panel with a card prop against the outside while drying
